log.why: E5 tests {metJ, katG}, which has combined prior probability near 0.46, maximizing expected information gain by splitting the probability mass nearly in half.
Treating at 3 uM splits the prior probability mass almost evenly (48% vs 52%), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
E6 tests araC and hisG together (~0.52 prior), which either isolates rpoB immediately or narrows the search to two genes.
Testing 1 µM splits the posterior evenly (0.513 vs 0.487) and strongly confirms 3 µM if no response occurs.
E8 splits the posterior nearly in half by testing the top candidate gyrA and lacZ (combined probability 0.541).
Test the top two candidates fliC and gyrA together (combined 0.526 prior) to split the probability mass efficiently.
Test gyrA directly on Ticket 3 so it can incubate while we publish Tickets 1 and 2.
With only 22 seconds left and rpoB at 0.737 posterior after excluding the other candidates, publishing now secures the points.
Start incubating E7 on Ticket 4 to split its top candidates (0.455 posterior) while we still have time to publish Ticket 2.
Ticket 2 has only 9 seconds left and 3 5M has a strong 0.697 posterior after positive E3 and negative E2 results.
Ticket 3 has only 8 seconds left and a very strong posterior (0.957) for gyrA after E3 confirmed phenotype loss.
Ticket 4 is low on time; testing katG (0.425) resolves the top two candidates ftsZ and katG.
Treating at 10 µM bisects the prior probability mass (52% at or below 10 µM vs 48% above) while waiting for Ticket 4's plate.
Ticket 4 has only 8 seconds left, so we must publish ftsZ (posterior 0.501) immediately before it expires.
E5 tests 30 µM, splitting the remaining probability mass evenly between <=30 µM and >=100 µM with time still left to publish.
Run E6 (100 µM) now so it finishes before the round ends if E5 is negative, while waiting for E5.
